fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. "when I summon them, they stand up together." (Isaiah 48:13) That's the same hand that founded the earth and spread out the heavens, and now they answer it as one. No late ones, no stragglers, and no one hitting snooze.

Yes, baker. "I have brought him, and he will succeed in his mission." (Isaiah 48:15) The LORD says this about His chosen ally from the verse before, the one who will carry out His desire against Babylon. He says it plainly, with no maybe in it.

Not this time, friend. The verse has no armies at all. The LORD says, "…your peace would have been like a river, and your righteousness like waves of the sea." (Isaiah 48:18) Think of a river that keeps on flowing and waves that keep on rolling in. That's the kind of peace and righteousness He's picturing.

Yes, baker. "their name would never be cut off or eliminated from My presence." (Isaiah 48:19) That's part of the same if only, right after the descendants as countless as the sand. Their offspring would be as numerous as its grains, and their name would still stand in His presence. A name that is never cut off is what He pictures.

Good guess, friend, but land isn't in this verse. The LORD says "their name would never be cut off or eliminated from My presence." (Isaiah 48:19) It comes right after the descendants as countless as the sand. I think it's a lovely thing to be told, that your name stays in His presence.

Not quite, baker, the temple isn't in this verse. The LORD says "their name would never be cut off or eliminated from My presence." (Isaiah 48:19) Right before it come the descendants, as countless as the sand. What stays in His presence here is their name.

Yes, baker. "The LORD has redeemed His servant Jacob!" (Isaiah 48:20) That's the news the verse says to proclaim out to the ends of the earth, with a shout of joy. Good news travels faster than the smell of fresh cookies.

That's right, baker. "They did not thirst when He led them through the deserts…" (Isaiah 48:21) The verse goes on, "He made water flow for them from the rock; He split the rock, and water gushed out." (Isaiah 48:21) So the answer is False, because they weren't left thirsty. Desert, yes. Thirst, no.
